title: Language Development: Skinner, Vygotsky, Chomsky, Bruner
summary: Behaviorist Theory (Skinner), Vygotsky's Theory, Chomsky's Innate Theory/LASS, Bruner's LASS, Universal Grammar, Transformational Grammar, Linguistic Relativity, Bruner's Cognitive Theory.
objectives: Describe Skinner's behaviorist theory of language.
Explain Chomsky's LAD and Universal Grammar.
Describe Vygotsky's social theory of language.
Explain Bruner's LASS and cognitive modes.
revision: Skinner: language learned through operant conditioning (mand, tact, echoic, intraverbal). Chomsky: LAD + Universal Grammar (innate). Vygotsky: social interaction and culture. Bruner: LASS + three representation modes (enactive, iconic, symbolic). Linguistic Relativity: language shapes thought.
confusions: Confusing Skinner (learning through reinforcement) with Chomsky (innate capacity).
Believing Vygotsky emphasized individual discovery over social interaction.

notes.t: B.F. Skinner proposed that language is learned through operant conditioning: reinforcement and imitation of adult speech.
Skinner identified verbal operants: mand (requesting), tact (labeling), echoic (repeating), and intraverbal (conversational).
Vygotsky emphasized social interaction and the role of culture in language development. Language and thought develop together through social interaction.
Noam Chomsky proposed that humans have an innate Language Acquisition Device (LAD) and Universal Grammar, enabling rapid language acquisition.
Jerome Bruner proposed the Language Acquisition Support System (LASS): the social environment that supports language learning through interaction.
Universal Grammar: innate principles common to all languages. Transformational Grammar: rules for transforming deep structure into surface structure.
The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis proposes that language shapes thought and perception.
Bruner proposed three modes of representation: enactive (action-based), iconic (image-based), and symbolic (language-based).
UGC NET frequently asks about Skinner's behaviorism, Chomsky's LAD, Vygotsky's social interaction, and Bruner's LASS.
